newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana expects 15th successive budget surplus.
newsitem.headline: Botswana expects 15th successive budget surplus.

text.p: Botswana's Finance Minister Festus Mogae said on Monday he expected a 763 million pula budget surplus in 1997/98 -- the 15th surplus in succession.

"Total revenues and grants of 7,815 million pula are expected to exceed total expenditures and net lending of 7,052 million pula, with a surplus of 763 million pula," Mogae said in his budget address to the National Assembly.
"Government cash balances will increase by 802 million pula," he added.

Mogae said 83.7 percent of revenues would come from the diamond-rich mineral sector, the Bank of Botswana, and customs and excise. Income tax is expected to contribute 5.7 percent of revenues and sales tax 3.5 percent.

In a bid to improve Botswana's investment potential, Mogae also said he was making cuts in income tax expected to cost 49.5 million pula over the year. "To attract investment and improve Botswana's international competitiveness, the tax system will be further streamlined," he said.

With effect from 1 July, 1997, the top personal marginal tax rate will drop from 30 percent to 25 percent and the level at which this will apply will be raised from 60,000 pula per annum to 80,000 pula. The threshold for income tax will be raised from 15,000 pula to 20,000 pula.

The proposed total recurrent budget is 4,873 million pula. The Ministry of Education will receive the largest share, 1,200 million pula or 25 percent. Local Government, Lands and Housing will get 983 million pula (20 percent) mainly for support grants to local authorities.
The Botswana Defence Force and the police will share 620 million pula, or 13 percent.

A development budget of 2,427 million pula is proposed. The largest spending will be on water, with the Ministry of Mineral Resources and Water Affairs getting 476 million pula for the North-South Water Carrier Project and village-level projects.
Mogae said the estimated budget outturn for 1996/97 (April-March) showed a surplus of 442 million pula, mainly due to exchange rate movements and an increase in diamond prices.
